plan.objective: Explain whether and how the chemical element mercury is hazardous to people.
plan.interpretation: Read "mercury" as the chemical element and explain its health effects, how the hazard differs by form, and how to reduce exposure.
assumptions: The question is about health risks to people, not to the environment in general.
plan.ambiguity_note: "Mercury" can also mean the planet, the Roman god, or a brand. This run assumes the chemical element because the question asks about danger. Ask again with more context if you meant something else.

documents.title: Health effects of exposure to mercury
documents.snippet: Exposure to high levels of mercury can harm the brain, kidneys, and developing fetus.
documents.content:
Health effects of exposure to mercury

Exposure to high levels of mercury can harm the brain, kidneys, and developing fetus. The effects depend on the form of mercury, the amount, and how a person is exposed.

Elemental mercury is most harmful when its vapor is inhaled, because the lungs absorb it efficiently. Methylmercury, the form that builds up in fish and shellfish, is the main source of mercury exposure for most people.

documents.title: Cleaning up a small mercury spill
documents.snippet: Do not use a vacuum cleaner on a mercury spill, because it spreads mercury vapor.
documents.content:
Cleaning up a small mercury spill

A small spill, such as from a broken thermometer, can usually be cleaned up by following official guidance. Larger spills should be reported to the local environmental or health agency.

Do not use a vacuum cleaner to clean up a mercury spill, because it spreads mercury vapor into the air.

documents.title: Eating fish while limiting mercury
documents.snippet: Choosing fish lower in mercury keeps the nutritional benefits of fish while limiting exposure.
documents.content:
Eating fish while limiting mercury

Fish is a good source of protein and other nutrients. Choosing fish lower in mercury lets pregnant people and young children keep the nutritional benefits of fish while limiting exposure.

Local advisories may give additional advice for fish caught in specific lakes and rivers.

documents.title: Mercury, the smallest planet
documents.snippet: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun.
documents.content:
Mercury, the smallest planet

Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun. Its surface temperature swings widely between day and night because it has almost no atmosphere.

Spacecraft have mapped its cratered surface in detail.

short_answer.text: Yes, mercury can be dangerous, but the risk depends on the form of mercury, the amount, and how a person is exposed. Exposure to high levels can harm the brain, kidneys, and a developing fetus. Inhaled mercury vapor and methylmercury in fish are the main concerns, and a vacuum cleaner should not be used on a spill because it spreads the vapor.

limitations: This answer assumes "mercury" means the chemical element.
The sources give general guidance; they do not replace advice from a poison control center or doctor after a specific exposure.
next_steps: If someone has been exposed, contact a poison control center or local health agency.
